title: Rolling capacity stress test and scope-gating for cycle-level staffing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Validate real-world capacity headroom across multiple service tiers during an active product cycle and create automated scope-gating rules that trim noncritical work when predicted capacity risk exceeds thresholds. This ticket coordinates a rolling stress-test plan, staffing ramp simulations, and the formalization of scope-gating criteria that PMs can rely on during mid-cycle reprioritization.

Scope:
- Run incremental load tests against the serving runtime under representative workload mixes (hosted API, Dedicated burst, Private VPC).
- Model staff availability scenarios (core team + surge lanes) and map these to a probabilistic capacity curve.
- Define gating rules (hard and soft) tied to observable signals: queue latency, tail p95/p99, model fallback rate, and predicted token cost over 1h and 24h horizons.
- Implement a lightweight playbook and a simple automation hook for console alerts that flag gated routes and recommended scope trims.

Out of scope: full implementation of autoscale engine changes (ENG follow-up ticket), and customer-facing messaging beyond documentation snippets in Console.

Rationale: Recent cycles exposed brittle cycle commitments when unexpected traffic or infra incidents consumed surge capacity. A repeatable stress-test + gating approach reduces surprise mid-cycle cut decisions and makes tradeoffs data-driven for PMs and ENG leads.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Completed rolling stress test matrix covering at least 3 workload profiles (interactive chat, batch embeddings, mixed read-heavy traffic) with documented results and annotated failure modes.
A2: A staffing-scenario spreadsheet mapping team allocations to expected throughput and latency ranges is uploaded and reviewed by Eng leads and PM org.
A3: Gating rules drafted (soft/hard thresholds) and encoded as a runbook + console alert spec; at least one gating rule is exercised in a dry-run and annotated in the runbook.
A4: A lightweight automation stub (alert -> recommended scope buckets) is merged to staging and linked to the Console dashboard; rollouts plan created for production integration.
A5: Post-mortem template and decision matrix included so future cuts record customer impact and rationale.
